# Wasserstein contraction of the augmented kernel {#sec-wasserstein-lifting}

A contracting Markov driver and a contractive memory update give geometric contraction of the full augmented process. The proof couples the driver trajectories and propagates their separation through the memory recursion.

## Coupling assumptions and the lifting theorem

Fix a parameter region $\mathsf K\subseteq\Theta$. The constants below may depend on $\mathsf K$, but not on $\theta\in\mathsf K$.

::: {#asm-driver-coupling}
## Geometrically contracting driver coupling

For every $\theta\in\mathsf K$ there is a Markovian coupling of two $P_\theta$-chains, with joint law denoted by $\mathbb{P}^\theta_{x,y}$, such that for every $n\geq0$ and $x,y\in\mathsf X$,

$$
\mathbb{E}^\theta_{x,y}d_X(X_n,\widetilde X_n)
\leq C_P\rho_P^n d_X(x,y),
\qquad C_P<\infty,\quad 0<\rho_P<1.
$$ {#eq-driver-trajectory-coupling}
:::

This is an estimate for one coupled pair of *trajectories*, at every time. A bound on $W_{d_X}(P_\theta^n(x,\cdot),P_\theta^n(y,\cdot))$ for each $n$, considered separately, does not by itself specify a consistent coupling of the intervening observations.

::: {#asm-memory-lipschitz}
## Spatial regularity and first moments for contractive memory

The memory update is uniformly contractive on $\mathsf K$ in the sense of @def-contractive-memory, with coefficient $r$. In addition, there is a constant $L_T<\infty$, independent of $\theta\in\mathsf K$, such that

$$
d_Y(T_\theta(x,u),T_\theta(y,u))\leq L_Td_X(x,y)
$$ {#eq-memory-spatial-lipschitz}

for all $x,y\in\mathsf X$ and $u\in\mathsf Y$.

For one, hence every, fixed $z_0\in\mathsf Z$, assume $Q_\theta(z_0,\cdot)\in\mathcal P_1(\mathsf Z)$.
:::

By the triangle inequality, memory contraction and spatial regularity together give

$$
d_Y(T_\theta(x,u),T_\theta(y,v))
\leq r\,d_Y(u,v)+L_Td_X(x,y).
$$ {#eq-memory-joint-lipschitz}

The one-step moment condition can be verified from a driver drift inequality and the growth of the memory forcing.

::: {#thm-wasserstein-lifting}
## Wasserstein contraction lifts through contractive memory

Suppose @asm-driver-coupling and @asm-memory-lipschitz hold. For every $\eta\in(\max\{\rho_P,r\},1)$ there is $C_Z(\eta)<\infty$, uniform in $\theta\in\mathsf K$, such that

$$
W_{d_Z}(Q_\theta^n(z,\cdot),Q_\theta^n(z',\cdot))
\leq C_Z(\eta)\eta^n d_Z(z,z'),
\qquad n\geq0.
$$ {#eq-augmented-contraction}

In particular $\tau_{d_Z}(Q_\theta^n)\leq C_Z(\eta)\eta^n$. Each $Q_\theta$ has a unique invariant distribution $\nu_\theta$ in $\mathcal P_1(\mathsf Z)$, and

$$
W_{d_Z}(\delta_zQ_\theta^n,\nu_\theta)
\leq C_Z(\eta)\eta^n W_{d_Z}(\delta_z,\nu_\theta).
$$ {#eq-invariant-wasserstein-rate}
:::

::: {.proof}
Fix $\theta$. Couple two driving paths according to @asm-driver-coupling, and evolve the corresponding memories using those paths. Put $e_n=\mathbb{E}^\theta_{x,y}d_Y(U_n,\widetilde U_n)$. By @eq-memory-joint-lipschitz and induction,

$$
e_n\leq r^n d_Y(u,v)
+L_T\sum_{j=1}^n r^{n-j}
\mathbb{E}^\theta_{x,y}d_X(X_j,\widetilde X_j).
$$

Together with @eq-driver-trajectory-coupling this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}^\theta_{x,y}d_Z(Z_n,\widetilde Z_n)
\leq {}& C_P\rho_P^n d_X(x,y)+r^n d_Y(u,v)\\
&+L_TC_P\sum_{j=1}^n r^{n-j}\rho_P^j d_X(x,y).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-memory-geometric-convolution}

For $\eta>\max\{r,\rho_P\}$, the geometric convolution satisfies

$$
\sum_{j=1}^n r^{n-j}\rho_P^j
=\eta^n\sum_{j=1}^n(r/\eta)^{n-j}(\rho_P/\eta)^j
\leq\frac{\rho_P}{\eta-\rho_P}\eta^n.
$$

Thus all three terms are bounded geometrically in $n$. The law of the coupled augmented paths is a coupling of the two $n$-step transition laws. Taking it as a candidate in the primal Wasserstein formula proves @eq-augmented-contraction.

At $n=1$ this gives $\tau_{d_Z}(Q_\theta)<\infty$. In conjunction with $Q_\theta(z_0,\cdot)\in\mathcal P_1$, the triangle inequality shows that $Q_\theta$ maps $\mathcal P_1(\mathsf Z)$ into itself. Choose $m$ such that $C_Z(\eta)\eta^m<1$. Then $\mu\mapsto\mu Q_\theta^m$ is a strict contraction on the complete space $(\mathcal P_1(\mathsf Z),W_{d_Z})$, so Banach's fixed-point theorem supplies a unique fixed point $\nu_\theta$. Since $\nu_\theta Q_\theta$ is also fixed by $Q_\theta^m$, uniqueness gives $\nu_\theta Q_\theta=\nu_\theta$. Finally, apply @eq-augmented-contraction to the coupling of $\delta_z$ and $\nu_\theta$.
:::

## First-moment verification

A driver drift inequality and the growth of the memory forcing provide a convenient way to verify augmented moment bounds.

::: {#lem-augmented-drift}
## Drift lifted through memory

Suppose the memory space is a subset of a normed space. For finite nonnegative constants $B,c_0,c_1$ and a measurable $w:\mathsf X\to[1,\infty)$, assume

$$
P_\theta w\leq aw+B,\qquad
\|T_\theta(x,u)\|\leq r\|u\|+c_0+c_1w(x),
\qquad 0\leq a,r<1.
$$ {#eq-driver-memory-drift}

Choose $\delta\in(\max\{a,r\},1)$ and $k>0$ sufficiently large that $(k+c_1)a\leq\delta k$. With

$$
\mathcal V(x,u)=1+kw(x)+\|u\|,
$$ {#eq-augmented-lyapunov}

the augmented transition satisfies

$$
Q_\theta\mathcal V\leq\delta\mathcal V+L,\qquad L<\infty.
$$ {#eq-augmented-drift}

:::

The calculation is given in [Appendix B](#sec-augmented-drift-proof).

With the norm metric on memory, if $w(x)$ is comparable to $1+d_X(x,x_0)$, this drift is naturally aligned with the first moment in $d_Z$. For an invariant law with finite $\mathcal V$-moment, invariance yields $\nu_\theta(\mathcal V)\leq L/(1-\delta)$. In the metric of @eq-product-metric, the corresponding first eccentricity is

$$
\int d_Z(z_0,z)\,\nu_\theta(dz)<\infty,
$$

as required for the $p=1$ Wasserstein Poisson theory of [@Hofstadler2026].
